mainTopic: The מרכבה vision: its creatures, angels and wings, contradictions between פסוקים, and the fiery river
overview: This amud keeps explaining the vision of the Divine Chariot (מרכבה) in ספר יחזקאל. It explains the word חשמל as fiery creatures that speak, or creatures that are silent when God speaks. It describes how the חיות run and return like flickering fire. רב says the stormy wind went to make נבוכדנצר ruler of the world, so ישראל would not be shamed by a lowly nation. A ברייתא names the angel סנדלפון, who ties crowns that rise to God by themselves. רבא says ישעיהו saw the same vision as יחזקאל but described it like a city dweller who is used to the king. The גמרא then settles several contradictions between פסוקים: the ox face that became a כרוב, six wings versus four, and the number of angels. Several of these are answered by the destruction of the בית המקדש, which reduced things in heaven too. Finally it discusses the fiery river, נהר דינור: it comes from the sweat of the חיות and pours onto the wicked, or onto 974 generations that were never created. That last teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: חשמל means speaking creatures of fire
steps.stepSummary: The word חשמל is read as a short form of three words: חיות אש ממללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word חשמל stands for 'speaking creatures of fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation of the word חשמל from the פסוק in יחזקאל. It reads the word as the first letters of three words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece of the word is treated as a separate word: ח for חיות, אש from the 'ש', and מל for ממללות. So the bright חשמל in the vision is really fiery creatures that speak.

keyTerms.meaning: A glowing substance in יחזקאל's vision, here read as a short form of three words
The holy creatures of the מרכבה

phrases.english: Speaking creatures of fire.
phrases.notes: This explains the word חשמל: ח from חיות, ש from אש, and מל from ממללות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation of חשמל begun just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חשמל = חיות אש ממללות, fiery creatures that speak.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the creatures are sometimes silent, sometimes speaking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא splits חשמל into חש (silent) and מל (speaking): they are silent when God speaks and speak when He does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: Sometimes they are silent and sometimes they speak. When God is speaking, they are silent. When God is not speaking, they speak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a second reading of the word חשמל. It splits the word into two halves that describe two different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here חש means 'silent' and מל means 'speak.' The creatures go quiet out of respect when הקדוש ברוך הוא speaks, and they sing or speak only when He is not speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
At times they are silent, at times they speak.
phrases.notes: Here the word חשמל is split in two: חש means silent and מל means speak.

phrases.english: When the divine speech goes out
from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, they are silent,
and when the divine speech does not go out
from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, they speak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second way to read the word חשמל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חשמל = חש (silent) and מל (speaking): silent while God speaks, speaking when He does not.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of חשמל: 'speaking fiery creatures' and 'silent/speaking' creatures.

steps.title: What does 'ran and returned' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the חיות running and returning like lightning and asks what 'ran and returned' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the creatures ran and returned like the look of a flash of lightning.' What does 'ran and returned' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק in the vision and asks about its first phrase. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is hard to picture creatures that run out and come back again and again. The גמרא wants a clear image of this movement.

phrases.english: "And the creatures ran and returned
like the appearance of a flash of lightning."
What is "ran and returned"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining a new פסוק in the same vision.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A picture of the 'running and returning' movement of the חיות.

steps.title: Like fire bursting out of a furnace
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the movement is like flames coming out of a furnace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Like fire that comes out of the mouth of a furnace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question with a picture from everyday life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flames at a furnace opening keep jumping out and pulling back. That is the 'run and return' movement of the חיות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Like fire that comes out of the mouth of the furnace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like flames that keep bursting out of a furnace and pulling back.

steps.title: What does 'like a flash of lightning' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the second phrase of the פסוק, כמראה הבזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like the appearance of a flash of lightning' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the second half of the same פסוק. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בזק is unusual, so the גמרא wants to know what picture it gives.

keyTerms.meaning: A flash; the גמרא connects it to flashing fire

phrases.english: What is "like the appearance of a flash of lightning"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word בזק in the פסוק.

steps.title: Like fire flashing between clay shards
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says it is like fire coming out from between pieces of pottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: Like fire that comes out from between broken pieces of pottery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers with another picture of fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When fire burns among broken clay pieces, it flashes out through the gaps. That gives the meaning of בזק, a quick bright flash.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
Like fire that comes out from between the shards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like fire flashing out from between clay shards.

steps.title: Where did the stormy wind go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening פסוק of the vision about a stormy wind from the north and asks where it went.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'I looked, and there was a stormy wind coming from the north, a great cloud, with fire flashing, a brightness all around it, and from inside it something like חשמל, from inside the fire.' Where did that wind go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק and asks where the stormy wind was going. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the wind 'came' but does not say where it was headed. The גמרא assumes it had a purpose and asks what it was.

phrases.english: "And I looked, and behold, a stormy wind
came out of the north, a great cloud,
and a fire flashing up, and a brightness around it,
and from its midst something like the color of electrum, from the midst of the fire."
Where did it go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the stormy wind.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the stormy wind from the north was headed.

steps.title: The wind went to conquer the world for נבוכדנצר
steps.stepSummary: רב says the wind went to put the whole world under the rule of נבוכדנצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It went to conquer the whole world and put it under the wicked נבוכדנצר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the wind was a power sent to give נבוכדנצר control of the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the stormy wind as a force sent out to make נבוכדנצר ruler of the whole world. The next steps explain why such a huge conquest was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked king of Babylonia who destroyed the first בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָלַךְ לִכְבּוֹשׁ אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
phrases.english: That it went to conquer the entire world
under the wicked Nebuchadnezzar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers where the wind went.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It went to conquer the whole world for נבוכדנצר.

steps.title: Why was all that needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why נבוכדנצר had to be made ruler of the entire world.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was all of this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why God would make a wicked king so powerful. This sets up the reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נבוכדנצר only needed to defeat ישראל, giving him the whole world seems like much more than was needed.

phrases.english: And why all of this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason behind רב's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why נבוכדנצר needed to rule the whole world.

steps.title: So the nations would not mock ישראל
steps.stepSummary: God made נבוכדנצר great so no one could say He handed His children to a lowly nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that the nations of the world would not say: The Holy One handed His children over to a low, unimportant nation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason: to protect the honor of ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ישראל was going to fall to נבוכדנצר anyway, God first made him a world ruler. That way their defeat was by a mighty empire and not a shameful one.

phrases.english: So that the nations of the world will not say:
Into the hand of a lowly nation

phrases.aramaic: מָסַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת בָּנָיו.
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, handed over His children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the conquest was needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To protect ישראל's honor, so their defeat would be by a great empire.

steps.title: The sins of ישראל made God serve idol worshippers
steps.stepSummary: God says that ישראל's sins caused Him to act as a servant for idol worshippers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One said: Who caused Me to become a servant to people who worship idols? The sins of ישראל caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this topic with God's own words, explaining who is to blame for this situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By helping נבוכדנצר win wars, God was in a sense working for an idol worshipper. He says this happened only because ישראל sinned and needed to be punished.
steps.whatToRemember: The stormy wind of the vision was the rise of נבוכדנצר, made great to protect ישראל's honor, and needed only because of ישראל's sins.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Who caused Me to be
an attendant to worshippers of idols?

phrases.aramaic: עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵן גָּרְמוּ לִי.
phrases.english: It was the sins of Israel that caused Me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the topic of the stormy wind with God's words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ישראל's sins are what caused God to help an idol-worshipping king.

steps.title: The 'one wheel' is a giant angel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the wheel on the earth is an angel standing on the ground whose head reaches the חיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'I looked at the creatures, and there was one wheel on the earth next to the creatures.' רבי אלעזר said: This is an angel who stands on the earth, and his head reaches up to the creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק from the vision, and רבי אלעזר explains what the 'wheel' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the wheel is both 'on the earth' and 'next to the חיות', who are high above. רבי אלעזר explains it as one huge angel who stands on the ground and reaches all the way up.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheel; also a kind of angel

phrases.english: "And I saw the creatures, and behold, one wheel
on the earth near the creatures,"
Rabbi Elazar said:
A certain angel who stands on the earth,
and his head reaches up next to the creatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'one wheel' is a giant angel standing on earth whose head reaches the חיות.

steps.title: A ברייתא names the angel סנדלפון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says this angel is סנדלפון, enormously tall, who stands behind the מרכבה and ties crowns for God.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: His name is סנדלפון. He is taller than his fellow angel by a distance of five hundred years. He stands behind the Chariot and ties crowns for his Creator.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds details about this angel: his name, his height, and his job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר only said the angel was huge. The ברייתא names him, gives his height, and says he makes crowns for God. This last detail is what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Sandalfon is his name,

phrases.aramaic: הַגָּבוֹהַּ מֵחֲבֵרוֹ מַהֲלַךְ חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: who is taller than his fellow by a distance of five hundred years.
phrases.notes: He means as far as someone could walk in five hundred years.

phrases.english: And he stands behind the Chariot
and ties crowns for his Maker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds details about the angel רבי אלעזר described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angel is סנדלפון; he stands behind the מרכבה and ties crowns for God.

steps.title: How can he crown God if no one knows His place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: a פסוק shows no one knows God's place, so how can an angel put a crown on Him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But it is written: 'Blessed is the glory of ה' from His place.' This shows that no one knows where His place is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the idea that סנדלפון ties crowns for God, using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels say 'from His place', not naming the place, which shows that even they do not know where God is. If so, how can סנדלפון bring a crown to Him?

phrases.english: Is that so?
But isn't it written: "Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place"?
This implies that there is no one who knows His place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's claim about the crowns.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that סנדלפון ties crowns for God.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no one knows God's place, an angel could not bring a crown to Him.

steps.title: The crown rises by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that סנדלפון says a name over the crown, and the crown goes up and rests on God's head by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says a name over the crown, and it goes and settles on His head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: סנדלפון does not need to know where God is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנדלפון only ties the crown and says a name over it. The crown finds its own way to God, so the angel never has to know God's place.
steps.whatToRemember: סנדלפון makes crowns for God but does not know His place; the crown rises to God by itself.

phrases.english: He says a name over the crown,
and it goes and sits on His head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the action happens so that the challenge no longer applies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the angel had to bring the crown to God himself, which would mean knowing His place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The angel says a name over the crown and it rises to God on its own.

steps.title: ישעיהו saw everything יחזקאל saw
steps.stepSummary: רבא says ישעיהו saw the same vision as יחזקאל, and explains with a parable why יחזקאל described it in so much more detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everything יחזקאל saw, ישעיהו saw too. יחזקאל is like a villager who saw the king. ישעיהו is like a city person who saw the king.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why יחזקאל's vision of the מרכבה is long and detailed while ישעיהו's is short, even though they saw the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not in what they saw but in how they reacted. A villager is amazed by everything and describes every detail. A city dweller is used to royalty and does not need to.

keyTerms.meaning: a villager, someone from a small town
a city dweller, someone from a big walled city
to what can it be compared? (opening of a parable)

phrases.english: Rava said:
All that Ezekiel saw, Isaiah saw.
To what may Ezekiel be compared?
To a villager who saw the king,
and to what may Isaiah be compared?
To a city dweller who saw the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כׇּל שֶׁרָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל, רָאָה יְשַׁעְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of סנדלפון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יחזקאל and ישעיהו saw the same vision. The difference in detail reflects how familiar each prophet was with the King's glory.

steps.title: A song to the One exalted above the exalted
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the doubled words 'גאה גאה' to mean that God is exalted over those who are themselves exalted.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does 'I will sing to ה׳, for He is גאה גאה' mean? It is a song to the One Who is exalted over the exalted ones.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains a פסוק from שירת הים. He reads the double wording 'גאה גאה' as 'exalted over the exalted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word is read as two levels. Some creatures are proud and exalted, and God is exalted above them. The next step will say who those exalted ones are.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
What is meant by that which is written:
"I will sing to the Lord, for He is highly exalted"?
A song to the One Who is exalted over the exalted ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected to the theme of God's glory over the מרכבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'גאה גאה' means God is exalted above the exalted creatures.

steps.title: The kings of the animals, and God above them all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports ריש לקיש with a teaching that lists the 'king' of each kind of creature, man above them, and God above everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: The king of wild animals is the lion, of domestic animals the ox, of birds the eagle. Man is exalted over them, and הקדוש ברוך הוא is exalted over all of them and over the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that shows who 'the exalted ones' are. These four, lion, ox, eagle and man, are exactly the four faces of the חיות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching builds a ladder: each animal is a king of its kind, man is above them, and God is above all. This gives a concrete meaning to 'exalted over the exalted.' It also leads into the next discussion about the faces of the חיות.

keyTerms.meaning: wild beasts (here). It is also the name of the angelic creatures of the מרכבה
as the Master said (introduces a supporting teaching)

phrases.english: As the Master said:
The king of the wild beasts is the lion,
the king of the domestic animals is the ox,
the king of the birds is the eagle,
and man is exalted over them,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְגָּאֶה עַל כּוּלָּן
phrases.english: and the Holy One, Blessed be He, is exalted over all of them
and over the entire world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports ריש לקיש's reading by identifying the 'exalted ones.'
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's reading of 'גאה גאה' as 'exalted over the exalted.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of the 'Master' listing the king of each kind of creature.

steps.title: Where did the ox face go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק lists an ox face among the חיות, but another lists a כרוב face instead and leaves out the ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says the faces were a man, a lion on the right, and an ox on the left. Another פסוק says the faces were a כרוב, a man, a lion and an eagle. The ox is not counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two פסוקים in יחזקאל side by side. They do not agree about the faces of the חיות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chapter 1 lists man, lion, ox and eagle. Chapter 10 lists כרוב, man, lion and eagle. The ox has been replaced by a כרוב, and the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: one פסוק says (opening of a contradiction between פסוקים)
it does not count / list it

phrases.english: One verse says:
"As for the likeness of their faces, the face of a man,
and the face of a lion on the right for the four of them,
and the face of an ox on the left for the four of them, etc."
And it is written:
"And each one had four faces:
the first face was the face of the cherub,
and the second face was the face of a man,
and the third the face of a lion,
and the fourth the face of an eagle,"
yet the ox is not counted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the list of the four creatures and turns to the faces of the חיות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two descriptions of the faces of the חיות in יחזקאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Chapter 1 includes an ox face, but chapter 10 has a כרוב in its place, so the פסוקים seem to contradict.

steps.title: יחזקאל prayed and the ox became a כרוב
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that יחזקאל prayed for the ox face to be changed, because it recalls ישראל's sin, and God turned it into a כרוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: יחזקאל asked for mercy about the ox face, and God turned it into a כרוב. יחזקאל had said: Master of the world, should an accuser become a defender?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains the contradiction as a real change. The ox face was there at first and was later replaced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are true, but they describe different times, before and after יחזקאל's prayer. The ox reminds of the עגל הזהב, so it 'accuses' ישראל. It should not stand before God in the place of those who speak in our favor.
steps.whatToRemember: The ox face of the חיות was changed to a כרוב because the ox recalls the עגל, and something that accuses should not serve as a defender.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Ezekiel asked for mercy about it,
and He turned it into a cherub.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
Shall an accuser become a defender?
phrases.notes: The ox brings to mind the עגל הזהב, which 'accuses' ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: יְחֶזְקֵאל בִּיקֵּשׁ עָלָיו רַחֲמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction about the missing ox.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different time periods: before and after יחזקאל's prayer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two lists seem to describe the same faces and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Originally there was an ox face. After יחזקאל's prayer it was turned into a כרוב.

steps.title: What is a cherub?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word כרוב means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'כרוב' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the ox became a כרוב, the גמרא asks what a כרוב looks like. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a question about the meaning of a word. It is asking for information, not raising a challenge.

phrases.english: What is "cherub"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the word introduced in ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and appearance of a כרוב.

steps.title: A cherub is like a child
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains כרוב as 'כרביא,' like a child, since in בבל a child is called 'רביא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: 'כרוב' means 'like a child,' because in בבל they call a child 'רביא.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers by splitting the word. 'כ' means 'like,' and 'רוב' sounds like 'רביא,' the word for a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as כ + רביא, 'like a child.' So the face of a כרוב is a child's face. The proof comes from how people in בבל speak.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Like a child,
phrases.notes: A wordplay: כ־רוב sounds like כ־רביא, "like a child."

phrases.english: for in Babylonia
they call a child "ravya."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word כרוב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כרוב has the face of a child.

steps.title: Then isn't a cherub face just a man's face?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: if a כרוב is a human child's face, why does the פסוק list a כרוב face and a man's face as two different faces?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, the פסוק lists a כרוב face, a man's face, a lion's face and an eagle's face. But a כרוב face would be the same as a man's face!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רבי אבהו's definition, using the very פסוק that lists the four faces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כרוב is a human face, the פסוק would be listing the same face twice. That cannot be right, since the פסוק counts four different faces.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (introduces a challenge from what was just said)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But if that is so,
that which is written:
"The first face was the face of the cherub,
and the second face was the face of a man,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי פְּנֵי אַרְיֵה וְהָרְבִיעִי פְּנֵי נָשֶׁר״,
phrases.english: and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle,"

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ פְּנֵי כְרוּב הַיְינוּ פְּנֵי אָדָם?
phrases.english: the face of a cherub is the same as the face of a man!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's definition of כרוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's definition that a כרוב is a child's face.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A child's face is a human face, so the פסוק would be listing 'man' twice.

steps.title: A big face and a small face
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that 'man' means a grown-up's big face, while 'כרוב' means a child's small face.
steps.simpleTranslation: A big face and a small face.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא's question in just a few words. The two faces are different sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are human faces, but one is an adult's and one is a child's. So they count as two different faces, and רבי אבהו's definition stands.

phrases.english: A big face and a small face.
phrases.notes: "Man" is an adult's face, and "כרוב" is a little child's face.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two similar things: an adult face versus a child's face.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כרוב face and a man's face would be identical.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man's face is a large adult face. A כרוב face is a small child's face.

steps.title: Six wings or four wings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that ישעיהו says each creature had six wings, while יחזקאל says each had four.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says: 'Six wings, six wings to each one.' Another פסוק says: 'Four faces to each one and four wings to each one of them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new contradiction between ישעיהו's vision and יחזקאל's vision, this time about the number of wings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said earlier that both prophets saw the same thing. So why does one count six wings and the other four?

phrases.english: One verse says:
"Six wings, six wings to each one,"
and another verse says:
"And every one had four faces,
and every one of them had four wings"?

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״שֵׁשׁ כְּנָפַיִם שֵׁשׁ כְּנָפַיִם לְאֶחָד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new contradiction about the creatures of the מרכבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The number of wings of the creatures in ישעיהו and יחזקאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says six wings and the other says four, so they seem to contradict.

steps.title: The wings shrank when the Temple was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that six wings describes the time the בית המקדש stands, and four wings describes the time it does not. As it were, the wings of the חיות were reduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it speaks of when the בית המקדש is standing. There, it speaks of when the בית המקדש is not standing. As it were, the wings of the חיות were reduced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each פסוק describes a different time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six wings is the full state, while the בית המקדש stands. Four wings is the reduced state after the חורבן. 'כביכול' signals that this is said carefully, about heavenly matters.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (opening of an answer)
as it were, so to speak

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are solved by a change over time. The ox became a כרוב after יחזקאל's prayer, and the wings went from six to four when the בית המקדש was destroyed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, when the Temple is standing,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there, when the Temple is not standing.
As it were, the wings of the creatures were reduced.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction about the number of wings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different time periods: before and after the חורבן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two prophets give conflicting counts of the wings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Six wings while the בית המקדש stands, and four after it is destroyed, because the wings were reduced.

steps.title: Which wings were taken away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which two of the six wings were removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which of the wings were taken away?
steps.whatsHappening: The last step said the חיות went from six wings to four. Now the גמרא asks which pair of wings they lost, and this sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו describes three pairs of wings: one pair covers the face, one covers the feet, and one is used to fly. Losing two wings means one of these three pairs is gone, so the גמרא wants to know which one.

phrases.english: Which of them were taken away?
phrases.notes: He means which of the wings. The last step said six wings went down to four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer that the wings were reduced from six to four.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which pair of the six wings was removed.

steps.title: רב: the wings they sang with
steps.stepSummary: רב says the lost wings are the ones the angels used while singing, and he proves it from a play on words between two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חננאל said in the name of רב: it was the wings they sing with. It says here, 'with two it flew, and one called to the other and said,' and it says elsewhere, 'Will you set your eyes on it? It is gone.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the angels lost the wings they used for flying while they sang שירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו, flying with two wings goes together with the angels calling out קדוש. The word for flying, יעופף, sounds like התעיף in משלי, where it means something that disappears. So רב reads the flying wings as the ones that 'flew away,' meaning they were lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Song, the angels' praise of הקדוש ברוך הוא
Will you set your eyes, or let it fly off? Here it describes something that vanishes

phrases.english: Rav Ḥananel said that Rav said:
Those with which they say song.
It is written here: 'And with two it flew,'
'and one called to the other and said,'
and it is written: 'Will you set your eyes on it? It is gone.'
phrases.notes: משלי 23:5. The word for flying here is linked to something that is gone, so those wings are what disappeared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of which wings were taken away.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wings used for flying while singing were the ones taken away.

steps.title: The רבנן: the wings that covered their feet
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the lost wings are the ones that covered the feet, because יחזקאל describes what the feet looked like.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: it was the wings they cover their feet with, as it says, 'and their feet were straight feet.' If those wings had not been taken away, how would he have known what the feet looked like?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a different answer: the angels lost the wings that covered their feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their proof is that יחזקאל, whose vision shows only four wings, describes what the angels' feet looked like. If the feet were still covered, he could not have seen them. So the foot-covering wings must be the ones that are gone.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Those with which they cover their feet,
as it is stated: 'And their feet were straight feet.'
And if they had not been taken away,
how would he have known?
phrases.notes: "He" means יחזקאל, who saw the feet and described them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question, which argues with רב's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wings covering the feet were taken away, since יחזקאל could see the feet.

steps.title: Maybe the feet were only uncovered for a moment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the feet were briefly uncovered so that יחזקאל could see them. After all, he also saw their faces, and nobody says the face-covering wings were lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe they were uncovered and he saw them. If you do not say so, then about 'the likeness of their faces was the face of a man,' would you also say those wings were taken away? Rather, they were uncovered and he saw them, and the same is true here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to knock down the רבנן's proof. It suggests that יחזקאל could have seen the feet during a moment when they were uncovered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument uses a comparison. יחזקאל also describes the faces, and the faces had covering wings too. Since everyone agrees those wings were not lost, he must have seen the faces when they were briefly uncovered. If that works for the faces, it should work for the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if you do not say this

phrases.english: Perhaps they were uncovered and he saw them.
Because if you do not say so,
then 'And the likeness of their faces was the face of a man'
would you also say that these were taken away?!
phrases.notes: He means the wings that covered the faces.

phrases.english: Rather, they were uncovered and he saw them;
here too, they were uncovered and he saw them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבנן's proof that came from יחזקאל seeing the feet.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected, not the רבנן's opinion itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Seeing the feet does not prove the wings were gone, because they could have been uncovered for a moment, just like the faces were.

steps.title: Faces and feet are not the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the רבנן: showing your face before your Master is respectful, but showing your feet is not, so the feet would never have been uncovered on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? His face is fine, since it is proper to uncover it before his Master. His feet are different, since it is not proper to uncover them before his Master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison from the last step, and in doing so it brings back the רבנן's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An angel would uncover its face before הקדוש ברוך הוא, because that is respectful. It would never uncover its feet, because that is not respectful. So the only way יחזקאל could have seen the feet is if the foot-covering wings were really gone.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on which wings were lost: רב says the wings used for singing and flying, and the רבנן say the wings that covered the feet. The רבנן's proof holds up, because feet would never be uncovered before הקדוש ברוך הוא out of respect.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אַפֵּיהּ — אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְגַלּוֹיֵי קַמֵּיהּ רַבֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Granted, his face: it is proper to uncover it before his Master.

phrases.aramaic: כַּרְעֵיהּ — לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְגַלּוֹיֵי קַמֵּיהּ רַבֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: His feet: it is not proper to uncover them before his Master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison between faces and feet, which brings back the רבנן's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison made in the last step.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Faces and feet are not alike. Uncovering the face is respectful, so it could happen for a moment. Uncovering the feet is not respectful, so it would not happen.

steps.title: Can the angels be counted or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction: one פסוק gives a number for the angels, and another says they cannot be counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says, 'A thousand thousands served Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him.' Another פסוק says, 'Is there a number to His troops?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new contradiction between two פסוקים, this time about how many angels serve הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דניאל gives a large but limited number. The פסוק in איוב says His troops cannot be numbered at all. Both cannot be true at the same time.

phrases.english: One verse says:
'A thousand thousands served Him,'
'and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him,'
and another verse says:
'Is there a number to His troops?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new contradiction between פסוקים, built the same way as the one about the wings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about how many angels there are.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק gives a set number, while the other says the angels cannot be counted at all.

steps.title: The heavenly entourage shrank after the חורבן
steps.stepSummary: Each פסוק describes a different time: angels without number while the בית המקדש stands, and a set number when it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it means when the בית המקדש stands, and there it means when the בית המקדש does not stand. It is as if the heavenly entourage was reduced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by assigning each פסוק to a different time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the בית המקדש stands, the angels are beyond counting, which is the פסוק in איוב. Once it is destroyed, their number goes down to the set amount in דניאל. This matches the answer about the wings: the חורבן made the heavenly world smaller as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; both can be true
As it were; said carefully when describing something about הקדוש ברוך הוא

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions, about the wings and about the number of angels, are answered the same way. When the בית המקדש is destroyed, things in heaven are reduced too.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the חורבן is not only a loss down here. As it were, the heavenly world is smaller too.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, when the Temple stands;
phrases.notes: "Here" is the פסוק saying there is no number.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים,
phrases.english: there, when the Temple does not stand;
as it were, the heavenly entourage was reduced.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction about how many angels there are.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: each פסוק describes a different period.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seemed to describe the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The number without limit applies while the בית המקדש stands, and the set number applies after the חורבן, when the heavenly entourage is reduced.

steps.title: The number counts only one troop
steps.stepSummary: אבא יוסי בן דוסאי says 'a thousand thousands' is the size of one troop of angels, but the number of troops has no limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי says in the name of אבא יוסי בן דוסאי: 'A thousand thousands served Him' is the number of one troop. 'And His troops have no number.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the contradiction from step 32. Both פסוקים are true because they are counting different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 solved the problem by pointing to different times. This answer points to different things being counted. Each troop has a fixed number (a thousand thousands), but nobody can count how many troops there are.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A troop or unit of angels
There is no number, it cannot be counted

phrases.english: It was taught: רבי says
in the name of אבא יוסי בן דוסאי:
'A thousand thousands served Him' —
is the number of one troop,
'and His troops have no number.'
phrases.notes: איוב 25:3. The number of troops is what cannot be counted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction that step 33 already answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different things are being counted: troop size versus number of troops
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים seem to count the total number of angels and disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק gives the size of a single troop. The other says the troops themselves are uncountable.

steps.title: The thousand thousands serve the fiery river
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says the 'thousand thousands' serve the נהר דינור, not ה׳ Himself, so ה׳'s servants can still be without number.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: 'A thousand thousands served it' means they serve the נהר דינור, as it says: 'A fiery river flowed and came out from before Him; a thousand thousands served it, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer to the contradiction. רבי ירמיה בר אבא reads the word 'him' in the פסוק as 'it,' meaning the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the full פסוק, the river is mentioned just before the angels. So 'served it' can mean the angels who serve the river. Those are counted. The angels who serve ה׳ Himself have no number.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'יְשַׁמְּשׁוּנֵּיהּ' here as 'served Him (ה׳‎).' רבי ירמיה בר אבא reads it as 'served it,' meaning the river.

phrases.english: And רבי ירמיה בר אבא said:
'A thousand thousands served it'
means the fiery river,
as it says: 'A fiery river flowed and came out'
from before Him; a thousand thousands served it,
and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate answer to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different subject: the counted angels serve the river, not ה׳
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'thousand thousands' are the total of ה׳'s servants.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the river's servants are counted. ה׳'s own servants are without number.

steps.title: Where does the fiery river come from?
steps.stepSummary: Since the river was just mentioned, the גמרא asks where it flows from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does it come out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side question about the נהר דינור. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק said the river 'came out from before Him.' The גמרא wants to know its actual source.

phrases.english: From where does it come out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the river mentioned in step 35 and asks about its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the נהר דינור

steps.title: From the sweat of the חיות
steps.stepSummary: The river comes from the sweat of the holy חיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the sweat of the חיות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 36.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חיות are the holy creatures that carry the heavenly throne, which the גמרא has been discussing. The fiery river is made from their sweat.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy creatures of the heavenly chariot

phrases.english: From the sweat of the חיות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The river flows from the sweat of the חיות.

steps.title: Where does the river pour out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the fiery river ends up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And to where does it pour?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the opposite question: where does the river go? This sets up two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After asking where it starts, the גמרא asks where it ends. Two אמוראים will answer differently.

phrases.english: And to where does it pour?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question about the same river.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the נהר דינור ends up

steps.title: Onto the heads of the wicked in גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב says the river pours onto the heads of the wicked in גיהנם and proves it from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: onto the heads of the wicked in גיהנם, as it says: 'Behold, a storm of ה׳ has gone out in fury, a whirling storm; it will whirl onto the head of the wicked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer to where the river goes, and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes ה׳'s fury landing 'on the head of the wicked.' רב reads this as the fiery river pouring onto them as punishment in גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the wicked are punished
It will whirl onto, land on

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said that רב said:
Onto the heads of the wicked in גיהנם,
as it says: 'Behold, a storm of ה׳ has gone out in fury,'
'a whirling storm;'
'it will whirl onto the head of the wicked.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The river pours onto the heads of the wicked in גיהנם.

steps.title: Onto those who were snatched away
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the river pours onto 'those who were snatched away,' based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: onto those who were snatched away, as it says: 'Who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a river.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to where the river goes. He learns it from a פסוק that mentions a river being poured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'those who were snatched away' with a 'river' that is 'poured.' רב אחא בר יעקב reads this river as the נהר דינור, pouring onto those people. Who they are is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Were snatched away, cut off early

phrases.english: And רב אחא בר יעקב said:
Onto those who were snatched away,
as it says: 'Who were snatched away before their time,'
'whose foundation was poured out as a river.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question that רב answered in step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The river pours onto 'those who were snatched away.'

steps.title: The 974 generations that were snatched away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי שמעון החסיד explains that 'those who were snatched away' are 974 generations that were supposed to be created.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון החסיד said: These are the 974 generations that were snatched away, that were supposed to be created...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains who the 'snatched away' people from step 40 are. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב did not say who 'those who were snatched away' are. רבי שמעון החסיד says they are 974 generations that were meant to be created. They are 'snatched away' because, as the continuing text will explain, they never came into the world.

phrases.english: It was taught: רבי שמעון החסיד said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת וְשִׁבְעִים וְאַרְבַּע דּוֹרוֹת
phrases.english: These are the nine hundred seventy-four generations
that were snatched away; they were to be created

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who 'those who were snatched away' in step 40 are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Those who were snatched away' are 974 generations that were meant to be created.
